summary:
Held 2 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 4 upside misses — SNDK +22%, TECH +20%, MU +16%, AMAT +13%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (AAPL -6%, TJX -6%, ROST -6%, DELL -6%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: SNDK (+21.97%) — Micron reported record Q3 revenue of $41.46B (+346% YoY) with $50B Q4 guidance after close June 25; SNDK surged ~22% as the closest NAND-peer beneficiary, with Citi raising its PT to $2,500. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — SNDK (~$2,335/share, ~4,000% YTD run) sits above typical price-cap and RSI thresholds; move was a sympathy trade on Micron earnings requiring sector-peer logic no current strategy carries.

top_movers.catalyst: Micron reported record Q3 revenue of $41.46B (+346% YoY) with $50B Q4 guidance after close June 25; SNDK surged ~22% as the closest NAND-peer beneficiary, with Citi raising its PT to $2,500.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SNDK (~$2,335/share, ~4,000% YTD run) sits above typical price-cap and RSI thresholds; move was a sympathy trade on Micron earnings requiring sector-peer logic no current strategy carries.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a MU-earnings-sympathy gate: when Micron beats revenue by ≥10% post-close, unlock NAND-peer tickers (SNDK) for the next session with RSI ceiling +10 pts and volume confirm ≥1.2× 20-day avg.

top_movers.catalyst: Activist Ananym Capital built a stake and urged Bio-Techne's board to pursue a sale or strategic review; amplified by TD Cowen reiterating Buy ($65 target) and Piper Sandler initiating at Neutral.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe; Bio-Techne (~$8B mid-cap life-science tools) falls outside sector/universe filters. Activist letter surfaced June 15 — move built over multiple sessions, requiring early positioning to capture.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 13D/13G activist-filing monitor; flag names with new >5% activist stakes and allow a universe exception if the name clears a momentum threshold within 10 trading days of the filing date.

top_movers.catalyst: Micron Q3 FY2026 beat: EPS $25.11 vs $20.20 est (+24%); Q4 revenue guidance ~$50B vs $43.6B consensus; data-center revenue +7× YoY on AI/HBM memory demand surge.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. MU gapped ~20% on June 24 earnings; a post-gap volatility or earnings-exclusion filter likely blocked re-admission, leaving the +15.74% continuation move on June 26 unreachable without a post-earnings re-entry rule.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings re-admission gate: names with ≥+15% earnings gap whose next-session close holds above the gap-day high and volume ≥1.5× 20-day avg may re-enter the momentum universe within 2 sessions of the catalyst date.

top_movers.catalyst: Micron Q3 earnings blowout (revenue $41.5B vs $35.7B est; EPS $25.11 vs $20.49 est) reported after-hours Jun 25 triggered a read-across rally in AMAT as the world's largest memory-fab equipment supplier; BofA, Wells Fargo, Citi all raised targets to $710–720.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AMAT is a large-cap ($250B+) semiconductor equipment name with no coverage. The move was a pre-open read-across from Micron's after-hours print; the full 13% gap was baked in at open before any intraday momentum or volume signal could form.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a read-across earnings trigger: when MU beats revenue by ≥10%, add AMAT/LRCX/KLAC to a pre-open watchlist and enter on a confirmed gap-up of ≥+5% within the first 30 minutes of the open, sized at half normal position given single-session gap risk.

top_movers.catalyst: Analyst PT upgrades (UBS to $228, Truist to $205) following Corning's multi-year multibillion-dollar optical fiber supply deal with Amazon for U.S. AI data centers and an Nvidia equity partnership, repricing GLW as core AI infrastructure supplier.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — GLW is a mega-cap industrials/materials name with no momentum or news-reactive sleeve coverage. The macro-aligned-macro-attn and regime-router strategies were exposed but GLW had already gained ~20% across Jun 20-24, almost certainly tripping RSI-overbought or cumulative-gap fil
top_movers.suggestion: Add a named-hyperscaler-contract flag to regime-router's entry gate: if a security has a disclosed multi-year supply agreement with a top-5 cloud/AI hyperscaler within the prior 5 sessions, exempt it from the RSI/gap ceiling and allow half-size entry, since analyst PT cascades reliably follow over subsequent sessions.

top_movers.catalyst: Micron reported FQ3 2026 revenue of $41.5B vs $36.5B est (+346% YoY) with $100B in new multi-year contracts, signalling a surge in HBM production that directly drives Teradyne memory-test equipment demand.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. TER is a large-cap semi-cap equipment name (~$69B) whose +10.5% move was a sympathy/read-through from Micron's after-hours print — a third-party earnings catalyst that pre-market positioning captures better than intraday signals.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'customer earnings read-through' trigger: when a disclosed major customer (e.g. MU) beats revenue consensus by ≥10%, flag semi-cap equipment suppliers (TER, AMAT, KLAC) for next-open momentum entry if they are not already in-universe.

top_movers.catalyst: Apple raised MacBook/iPad prices 18–25% mid-cycle, citing AI-driven memory cost inflation ('hundred-year flood' per CEO Cook), stoking demand-destruction fears and a broad margin-squeeze narrative.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AAPL's mega-cap status excludes it from current scope. Move was catalyst-driven by a product-pricing press release; post-close momentum signals arrived too late to capture the gap.
top_movers.suggestion: Add AAPL to a catalyst watchlist: gate a momentum-short entry when a product-pricing press release drives a pre-market gap ≥4% (or express via QQQ inverse proxy if short capability is unavailable).

top_movers.catalyst: Insider sell-off: Chairman Meyrowitz sold 21.6% of her stake (~$9.1M) and CEO Herrman ~$12M in early June; Form 4 disclosures circulated June 25–26, amplified by elevated PCE inflation data and a stretched 30× forward-PE premium.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (large-cap consumer discretionary, ~$170B market cap). Even if in-universe, the move was Form 4 disclosure-driven — a multi-day drift without a single-session gap or volume spike that momentum or news-reactive filters require.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change for long-only strategies — missing a loser is the correct outcome. If a market-neutral sleeve exists, add a Form-4 signal (C-suite sale >15% stake within 30 days) as a short-entry trigger for large-cap consumer discretionary.

top_movers.catalyst: Wells Fargo cut ROST to Equal Weight on Jun 23 citing stretched valuation after ~80% YoY rally; selling extended through Jun 26, amplified by Q1 tariff-margin warnings (~50% China sourcing, Q2 EPS hit $0.11–$0.16).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ROST is a large-cap (~$71B) consumer discretionary off-price retailer not covered by sector screens. The move was analyst-downgrade-driven with a 3-day lag, favouring pre-positioning over reactive signals.
top_movers.suggestion: Add off-price retail peers to a consumer discretionary watchlist with a downgrade-momentum short gate: flag when a mega-cap is cut to Hold after >60% 12-month rally and price confirms >2% below the downgrade day's close within one session.

top_movers.catalyst: GF Securities downgraded DELL Buy→Hold on Jun 25, citing ~34× P/E vs 13× historical median; AI revenue upside seen as fully priced in, amplified by $1.56B insider selling and ODM-direct customer disintermediation risk.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — DELL is a large-cap AI-infrastructure hardware name not covered by current strategies. The move was catalyst-driven (analyst downgrade published pre-market Jun 25), requiring positioning before the signal rather than reacting to a technical setup.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a news-reactive short gate: names with analyst Buy→Hold/Sell downgrade + P/E > 2× 5yr median + net insider selling > $500M/90d enter a 1-session mean-reversion short list; back-test on large-cap hardware (DELL, HPE, SMCI) before enabling.
